:::{#exm-cauchy-no-mean}
#### The standard Cauchy distribution has no expectation

Let $X$ have the standard Cauchy distribution,
with density $\p(X=x) = \frac{1}{\pi(1 + x^2)}$ for every real $x$.
For $x \ge 0$, $\frac{1}{2\pi}\log(1 + x^2)$ is an antiderivative of
$\abs{x} \cd \frac{1}{\pi(1 + x^2)} = \frac{x}{\pi(1 + x^2)}$,
and for $x \le 0$, $-\frac{1}{2\pi}\log(1 + x^2)$ is an antiderivative of
$\abs{x} \cd \frac{1}{\pi(1 + x^2)} = \frac{-x}{\pi(1 + x^2)}$.
So, integrating over each half-line:

$$
\ba
\int_{0}^{\infty} \abs{x} \cd \frac{1}{\pi(1 + x^2)}\,dx
&= \lim_{b \to \infty} \sb{\frac{1}{2\pi}\log(1 + x^2)}_{0}^{b}
&& \text{(antiderivative on } [0, \infty) \text{)} \\
&= \lim_{b \to \infty} \frac{1}{2\pi}\log(1 + b^2)
&& \text{(evaluate at the bounds; } \log 1 = 0 \text{)} \\
&= \infty
&& \text{(} \log(1 + b^2) \to \infty \text{ as } b \to \infty \text{)}
\ea
$$

$$
\ba
\int_{-\infty}^{0} \abs{x} \cd \frac{1}{\pi(1 + x^2)}\,dx
&= \lim_{a \to -\infty} \sb{-\frac{1}{2\pi}\log(1 + x^2)}_{a}^{0}
&& \text{(antiderivative on } (-\infty, 0] \text{)} \\
&= \lim_{a \to -\infty} \frac{1}{2\pi}\log(1 + a^2)
&& \text{(evaluate at the bounds; } \log 1 = 0 \text{)} \\
&= \infty
&& \text{(} \log(1 + a^2) \to \infty \text{ as } a \to -\infty \text{)}
\ea
$$

Both halves diverge,
so $\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \abs{x} \cd \frac{1}{\pi(1 + x^2)}\,dx$ diverges,
and by @def-expectation, $X$ has no expectation.

:::
